t: A father buys a health policy and his adult son, covered under it, uses the hospital cashless service with the father's approval. Under Section 2(7) the son is:
o: A consumer only if he is a co-payer of premium
A consumer only after the father's death
Not a consumer, as he paid no consideration
A consumer, being a beneficiary of services availed with the approval of the person who hired them
e: Section 2(7)(ii) includes any beneficiary of services other than the person who hires them, when the services are availed with the approval of the first-mentioned person.

t: Which of the following modes of purchase was specifically brought within the definition of 'consumer' by the 2019 Act, closing a gap in the 1986 Act?
o: Purchases through online, teleshopping, direct selling and multi-level marketing
e: The 2019 Act widened the definition to cover goods bought through offline or online transactions, electronic means, teleshopping, direct selling or multi-level marketing, which the 1986 Act did not specifically include.

t: A manufacturer gave an express warranty that its water purifier removes all bacteria. It fails to do so and a buyer falls ill. The manufacturer proves it was neither negligent nor fraudulent in making the warranty. Under the 2019 Act the manufacturer:
o: Remains liable in the product liability action despite proving absence of negligence or fraud
Is liable only if the seller is also found negligent
Is liable only to refund the price
Escapes liability, having proved absence of negligence
e: The Act makes manufacturers liable in a product liability action even where they prove they were not negligent or fraudulent in making the express warranty, placing a higher burden on manufacturers than on sellers or service providers.

t: A buyer modifies a mixer-grinder motor to run at higher speed and is injured when it bursts. In a product liability action against the retailer, the retailer's best defence under the 2019 Act is that:
o: The product was sold at a discount
The manufacturer is a foreign company
The retailer is only a platform
The product was altered or modified by the buyer
e: The Act exempts the product seller from liability where the product has been misused, altered or modified by the consumer.

t: An insurer's call centre passes a policyholder's health details, given in confidence in the proposal form, to a third-party marketing firm without any legal requirement. Under the 2019 Act this is:
o: A deficiency only if a loss occurs
Permissible as part of customer service
e: The 2019 Act's definition of unfair trade practice specifically includes disclosure of personal information given by a consumer in confidence, unless the disclosure is made in accordance with any other law.

t: The 2019 Act fixes liability on endorsers of advertisements primarily because:
o: Endorsers are treated as product manufacturers
Advertising agencies are not legal persons
Endorsers receive a share of sales revenue
Consumers have fallen prey to unfair trade practices under the influence of celebrities, so endorsers must exercise due diligence
e: The Act expects endorsers to verify the veracity of claims they endorse; absent due diligence they share liability for misleading advertisements.

t: A complaint alleging an unfair contract where the consideration paid is ₹8 crore lies before the:
e: For unfair contracts the State Commission has jurisdiction where consideration does not exceed ₹10 crore (Section 47(1)(a)(ii)); beyond ₹10 crore it goes to the NCDRC under Section 58(1)(a)(ii).

t: The NCDRC's original jurisdiction over consumer complaints under Section 58(1)(a)(i) arises where the consideration paid exceeds:
e: Complaints where the value of goods or services paid as consideration exceeds ₹2 crore lie before the National Commission.

t: A policyholder's claim was repudiated on 15 March 2024. The last date for filing a consumer complaint within the normal limitation under Section 69 is:
e: Section 69 allows two years from the date the cause of action arose; two years from 15 March 2024 ends on 14 March 2026. Thereafter a condonation application is required.

t: A revision petition before the State Commission under Section 47(1)(b) must be filed within:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Regulation 14(1)(i) of the Consumer Protection (Consumer Commission Procedure) Regulations, 2020 prescribes 90 days for revision petitions before the State Commission and the NCDRC.

t: An appeal from the State Commission's order in a consumer complaint lies to the NCDRC under Section 51(1) within:
e: Section 51(1) provides 30 days for appeal to the NCDRC, with power to condone delay; the 45-day period applies to appeals from the District to the State Commission.

t: A review petition against an order of the NCDRC is filed under Section 60 within:
e: Section 60 read with Regulation 14(1)(iii) of the Consumer Commission Procedure Regulations, 2020 prescribes 30 days for review before the NCDRC, as for the District (Section 40) and State (Section 50) Commissions.

t: The alternative dispute resolution mechanism introduced by the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 to reduce pendency in consumer courts is:
e: The 2019 Act provides for mediation, with mediation cells attached to Commissions, so that disputes may be settled faster and the load on consumer courts reduced.

topic: MV Act s.147 – Requirements of policy
t: Under Section 147(1)(b)(i), third-party liability must be covered in respect of accidents caused by or arising out of the use of the vehicle:
e: The compulsory cover under Section 147(1)(b)(i) is for death, bodily injury or third-party property damage arising out of use of the vehicle in a public place.

t: Before the 2019 amendment, Section 147(1)(b)(ii) required cover for death or bodily injury of passengers of:
e: The un-amended clause referred to passengers of a public service vehicle; the 2019 amendment widened it to passengers of a transport vehicle, excluding gratuitous passengers of a goods vehicle.

t: The conductor of a stage carriage dies in an accident while on duty. The insurer's compulsory liability under Section 147 for his death is:
o: Nil, as he is an employee
Limited to the liability arising under the Workmen's/Employees' Compensation Act, 1923
Unlimited, as for any third party
e: The proviso to Section 147(1) exempts the policy from covering employee death in the course of employment except for liability under the Compensation Act, for drivers, conductors/ticket examiners of a public service vehicle and employees carried in a goods carriage.

topic: MV Act s.147 – Limits of liability
t: Under the un-amended Section 147(2)(a), the policy must cover liability for death or bodily injury of a third party up to:
e: Section 147(2)(a) required cover for 'the amount of liability incurred', i.e. unlimited, whereas clause (b) fixed ₹6,000 for third-party property damage.

t: The 2019 amendment to Section 166 reintroduced a limitation period for filing a claim application before the Claims Tribunal of:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 166(3) as inserted in 2019 provides that no application for compensation shall be entertained unless made within six months of the occurrence of the accident.

t: Under the proviso to the old Section 147(2), a limited-liability policy in force immediately before commencement of the 1988 Act continued to be effective for:
o: Four months after commencement or till expiry, whichever earlier
Till expiry of the policy in all cases
e: The transitional proviso allowed such policies to continue for four months after commencement of the Act or till the date of expiry of the policy, whichever was earlier.

t: An insurer issued a three-year two-wheeler liability policy on 1 July 2019, before the 2019 Amendment Act commenced on 1 September 2019. Under the amended Section 147(4) this policy:
o: Must be re-issued on amended terms
Continues on its existing terms as if the Act had not been amended
Continues only if the premium is topped up
e: Amended Section 147(4) provides that a policy issued before commencement of the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 continues on the existing contractual terms and the Act applies as if it had not been amended.

t: When a cover note is not followed by a policy within the specified time, the insurer's notification under Section 147 goes to:
o: The registering authority or such other authority as the State Government may prescribe
The Regional Transport Officer of the insurer's head office
e: The notification must be made to the registering authority in whose records the vehicle is registered, or to any other authority prescribed by the State Government.

t: Section 147(5)/(6) provides that, notwithstanding any other law, an insurer issuing a policy under the section shall:
o: Be liable to indemnify the persons specified in the policy for the liability it purports to cover
Be liable only after the insured pays the award
Be liable only up to the premium collected
Have no liability if the insured breaches policy conditions
e: The sub-section makes the insurer liable to indemnify the person or classes of persons specified in the policy in respect of any liability the policy purports to cover, overriding any other law.

t: The amended Section 147(2) refers to prescribing a base premium for third-party insurance in respect of:
o: Death or grievous hurt to a person
e: The amended sub-section covers third-party insurance related to either death of a person or grievous hurt, for which the Central Government prescribes a base premium and insurer's liability.

t: Which of these is NOT among the employee categories listed in the proviso to Section 147(1)?
o: Employee engaged in driving the vehicle
Conductor of a public service vehicle
Employee being carried in a goods carriage
Mechanic repairing the vehicle in the insured's garage
e: The proviso names drivers, conductors/ticket examiners of a public service vehicle and employees carried in a goods carriage; a garage mechanic is not listed.

t: Before the 2019 amendment, the no-fault compensation under Section 140 for death and permanent disablement was:
e: Section 140 (now omitted) provided ₹50,000 for death and ₹25,000 for permanent disablement without proof of fault; Section 164 now provides ₹5 lakh and ₹2.5 lakh.

t: Under the amended Section 149, after receiving information of an accident from the police, the insurer must designate an officer to settle the claim and make an offer to the claimant within:
e: Amended Section 149 requires the insurer's designated officer to make an offer of settlement within 30 days of receipt of the accident information; if accepted, payment follows within 30 days.

t: Although Section 30 of the Indian Contract Act makes wagering agreements void, an insurance contract is enforceable because:
o: The premium is paid in advance under Section 64VB
The insured has an insurable interest in the subject matter
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Insurable interest distinguishes insurance from a wager: the insured stands to lose on the happening of the event, so the contract is one of indemnity, not a bet.

t: A person drives a vehicle on a public road without a valid third-party insurance policy. Under Section 196 (as amended in 2019) the penalty for a first offence is:
o: Imprisonment up to 6 months or fine of ₹10,000
Imprisonment up to 3 months or fine of ₹1,000 or both
Imprisonment up to 3 months or fine of ₹2,000 or both
e: Section 196 provides imprisonment up to three months or a fine of ₹2,000 or both for the first offence; a subsequent offence attracts a fine of ₹4,000.

t: A Claims Tribunal award is for ₹80,000. Can the insurer appeal to the High Court under Section 173?
o: No, as no appeal lies where the amount in dispute is less than ₹1 lakh
e: Section 173(2), as amended in 2019, bars an appeal where the amount in dispute in the appeal is less than ₹1,00,000 (earlier ₹10,000).

t: Under Section 166(2), an application for compensation may be filed before the Claims Tribunal having jurisdiction over the area where:
o: Only the insurer's head office is situated
The accident occurred, or the claimant resides or carries on business, or the defendant resides
e: Section 166(2) gives the claimant the option of the Tribunal of the area of the accident, of the claimant's residence/business, or of the defendant's residence.

t: A premium cheque is received by a branch on 5 April and credited on 8 April. Under Section 64VB and the Insurance Rules, the risk may be assumed from:
o: 5 April, the date the cheque was received, provided it is honoured
The date the policy is printed
1 April, the start of the financial year
e: Where premium is paid by cheque, the risk may be assumed from the date the cheque is received/delivered, subject to realisation; if the cheque is dishonoured the policy is void ab initio.

t: Section 38 of the Insurance Act, 1938 deals with:
o: Assignment and transfer of insurance policies
e: Section 38 governs assignment or transfer of a policy by endorsement or separate instrument; Section 39 deals with nomination and Section 41 with rebates.

t: A surveyor appointed on a ₹4 lakh fire claim files her report. Under Section 64UM, the surveyor's report is:
o: Binding only if the claim exceeds ₹1 lakh
Binding on the insurer in all respects
Not binding; the insurer may settle for a different amount but must record reasons
Binding on the insured but not on the insurer
e: Section 64UM makes the survey report a mandatory input for claims above the threshold, but it does not bind the insurer, which may deviate for recorded reasons and must still settle within the prescribed time.

t: Under Section 101A of the Insurance Act, 1938 read with IRDAI notification, the obligatory cession by Indian general insurers to GIC Re for recent years is:
e: IRDAI fixes the obligatory cession to the Indian reinsurer (GIC Re) under Section 101A; it has been 4% since 2022-23.

t: Section 64VB(4) of the Insurance Act, 1938 requires that any refund of premium due to the insured must be paid:
o: By crossed or order cheque, postal money order or electronic transfer directly to the insured
Through the agent who procured the policy
e: Section 64VB(4) mandates that refunds be paid directly to the insured by crossed or order cheque, postal money order or electronic transfer, and not through intermediaries.

t: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999 was passed to:
o: Establish a regulator to protect policyholders' interests and regulate, promote and ensure orderly growth of the insurance industry
Merge the four PSU general insurers
e: The IRDA Act, 1999 set up the Authority (constituted in April 2000) to protect policyholders and to regulate, promote and ensure the orderly growth of insurance and reinsurance business, opening the sector to private players.

t: The permitted limit of foreign direct investment in an Indian insurance company is currently:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Raised from 49% to 74% by the Insurance (Amendment) Act 2021; intermediaries may have 100%.

t: Under the IRDAI 2024 policyholder-protection framework, an insurer must communicate its decision on a proposal within how many days of receiving the proposal with all requirements?
e: The 2024 regulations require insurers to decide on the proposal within 7 days of receipt of the proposal and all necessary documents, and to issue the policy in electronic form.

t: A general insurer settles a claim 60 days after the date it should have been paid under the regulations. Under the PPHI framework the insurer must pay interest on the delayed amount at:
o: 2% above the bank rate prevailing at the beginning of the financial year
e: The policyholder-protection regulations require insurers to pay interest at 2% above the bank rate for delays beyond the prescribed timelines, over and above the claim amount.

t: Once the Insurance Ombudsman passes an award and the complainant accepts it, the insurer must comply within:
e: The award is binding on the insurer, which must comply within 30 days of receipt of the award and inform the Ombudsman; the complainant is not bound and may approach other fora.

t: The Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 imposes on the owner handling a hazardous substance a liability that is:
o: No-fault, i.e. relief is payable without the victim proving negligence
Limited to employees of the owner
e: Section 3 makes the owner liable to give relief for death, injury or property damage from an accident involving a hazardous substance without the claimant having to plead or prove fault.

t: A claim for relief under the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 is made to the:
e: Applications for relief are made to the Collector of the district, who holds an inquiry and makes an award; the application must be filed within five years of the accident.

t: A 40-year-old employee (relevant factor 184.17) earning ₹12,000 per month suffers permanent total disablement. Compensation under the Employees' Compensation Act is:
e: Permanent total disablement = 60% of monthly wages × relevant factor, or ₹1,40,000, whichever is more. 60% × 12,000 × 184.17 = ₹13,26,024 (wages are below the ₹15,000 cap).

t: An injured workman is off duty for 5 days due to an accident at work. Under the Employees' Compensation Act, temporary disablement compensation is payable:
o: For all 5 days at full wages
Only if disablement exceeds 3 days, as half-monthly payments of 25% of monthly wages
Not at all, as temporary disablement is excluded
e: No compensation is payable for injury that does not result in disablement exceeding three days; beyond that, temporary disablement attracts half-monthly payments of 25% of monthly wages.

t: Under Section 11 of the Indian Contract Act, a proposer is competent to contract if he:
o: Has attained 18 years, is of sound mind and is not disqualified by law
e: Section 11 requires majority (18 years under the Majority Act), sound mind and absence of legal disqualification; a policy proposed by a minor is void.

t: Under the IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests) Regulations 2024, the free-look period for a policy with a term of one year or more is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). 30 days from receipt of the policy document, irrespective of the sales channel.

t: A fire policy condition states that if a claim is not pursued within 12 months of rejection it shall be deemed abandoned. Which provision of the Indian Contract Act is relevant to the validity of such a clause?
e: Section 28 (as amended in 1997) renders void agreements that limit the time for enforcing rights or extinguish rights on expiry of a specified period; such policy clauses are tested against it.

t: Under Rule 9 of the PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, which of the following is an Officially Valid Document for KYC of an individual policyholder?
o: Passport, driving licence, Aadhaar, voter ID, NREGA job card or NPR letter
e: The six OVDs are passport, driving licence, proof of possession of Aadhaar, Voter's Identity Card, NREGA job card and the letter issued by the National Population Register.

t: A customer offers to pay a fleet policy premium of ₹2.5 lakh in cash. The branch should:
o: Accept, as cash is legal tender
Decline cash of ₹2 lakh or more in view of Section 269ST of the Income-tax Act and AML norms, and insist on a non-cash mode
Accept and file a Suspicious Transaction Report
e: Section 269ST bars receipt of ₹2 lakh or more in cash in aggregate from a person in a day/transaction; AML norms also require PAN/Form 60 for cash above ₹50,000.

t: The fee for filing an application under the Right to Information Act, 2005 with a Central public authority such as a PSU insurer is:
e: The RTI (Regulation of Fee and Cost) Rules prescribe ₹10 as the application fee; persons below the poverty line are exempt from fee.
